name: Mortgage rate
seoDesc: Mortgage rate: work out mortgage points from the loan balance and the mortgage term. A free finance calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the loan balance, the mortgage term, the mortgage rate and the expected interest rate at the last period and the Mortgage rate calculator solves for mortgage points. It is built for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Mortgage rate calculator work?
sections.html:
The Mortgage rate calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports mortgage points in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the compounding frequency and the mortgage type); then you type in the loan balance, the mortgage term, the mortgage rate and the expected interest rate at the last period.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Mortgage rate calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Mortgage points=up-front fee ÷ loan balance
Monthly payment=(mortgage rate, mortgage term, M, Q, loan balance, mortgage points, annual fee, expected adjustment, periods between adjustments, interest rate cap, interest rate floor, first adjustment after..., expected interest rate at the last period, var int adj, var type)
Adjusted mortgage rate (APR)=(mortgage rate, mortgage term, M, Q, loan balance, mortgage points, annual fee, expected adjustment, periods between adjustments, interest rate cap, interest rate floor, first adjustment after..., expected interest rate at the last period, var int adj, var type)
Paid interest=(mortgage rate, mortgage term, M, Q, loan balance, mortgage points, annual fee, expected adjustment, periods between adjustments, interest rate cap, interest rate floor, first adjustment after..., expected interest rate at the last period, var int adj, var type)
Total payments=(mortgage rate, mortgage term, M, Q, loan balance, mortgage points, annual fee, expected adjustment, periods between adjustments, interest rate cap, interest rate floor, first adjustment after..., expected interest rate at the last period, var int adj, var type)
Additional costs=(mortgage rate, mortgage term, M, Q, loan balance, mortgage points, annual fee, expected adjustment, periods between adjustments, interest rate cap, interest rate floor, first adjustment after..., expected interest rate at the last period, var int adj, var type)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Time, opening in years
  • %, opening in percent
  • %, opening in percent
  • %, opening in percent
  • Time, opening in years
  • Time, opening in months
  • %, opening in percent

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Mortgage rate calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Preparing questions for a lender, an accountant or an adviser
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the loan balance, the mortgage term and the mortgage rate — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Mortgage rate calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns mortgage points, derived from the loan balance, the mortgage term and the mortgage rate. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Mortgage rate calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the loan balance, the mortgage term, the mortgage rate and the expected interest rate at the last period, which is 15 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter loan balance in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Loan balance opens in US Dollar and the chip beside it offers 113 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Mortgage rate calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
